name: Nuclino
description: Teams, workspaces, items, collections, fields, and files through Nuclino's hosted MCP.
agentUseSummary: Connect once through Nuclino OAuth, then let agents use every documented read or write MCP tool under Safe or Dangerously skip permissions.

capabilities.label: Read workspace knowledge
capabilities.description: List teams and workspaces, search and read items, and retrieve attached-file metadata.

capabilities.label: Create and maintain knowledge
capabilities.description: Create, update, edit, or trash items and collections and manage workspace fields.

allowed.label: Use read tools
allowed.description: Use one exact documented Nuclino MCP read tool with bounded arguments and live schema validation.

approvalRequired.label: Use write tools
approvalRequired.description: Use one exact documented Nuclino MCP mutation tool; Safe mode requires approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: Documented reads run directly; every create, update, edit, trash, or field mutation requires approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: Every selected OAuth-authorized Nuclino MCP operation runs without Relay per-action approval; ownership, provider permissions, exact tool allowlists, bounds, audits, schema validation, and rate limits still apply.

runtimeSupport.description: Railway mounts exact read/write wrappers and proxies Nuclino OAuth to its hosted MCP.
Railway mounts exact read/write wrappers and proxies Nuclino OAuth to its hosted MCP.

providerSetup.blocker: Relay's public PKCE client is dynamically registered with the exact Railway callback, but no signed-in Nuclino user session was available for production OAuth and action acceptance.
providerSetup.nextAction: A Nuclino user clicks Connect, approves the MCP connection, then Relay runs callback, MCP health, a bounded search, and an approved or Dangerous-mode mutation.

evidence.supports: Nuclino documents its hosted MCP at https://api.nuclino.com/mcp, OAuth 2.0 with PKCE, account-permission enforcement, revocation, and the complete current read/write tool list.
Nuclino publishes authorization, token, and dynamic registration endpoints with authorization-code and S256 PKCE support.
Nuclino's separate REST API uses customer-owned API keys with the same authority as the account; Relay prefers the official one-click hosted MCP OAuth route.
Nuclino documents bounded list, search, read, create, update, and trash semantics for items and collections.
